content: 1. Lesinurad reduces the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Patients should use additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods and not rely solely on hormonal contraception while taking lesinurad. 2. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effectiveness of letrozole due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Concurrent use of letrozole with estrogens or estrogen-containing products should be avoided. 3. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor closely for arrhythmias and related events, as its effect on the QT interval is unknown. 5. Lopinavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control in this case. 7. Mavacamten decreases systemic exposures of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add non-hormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 8. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Discontinuation of estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration may be advisable. 9. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral and ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Its use is contraindicated. 10. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 11. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Nelfinavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 14. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral and ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may not be effective due to weak CYP3A4 induction. 15. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 16. Perampanel reduces levonorgestrel levels by 40% when coadministered at high doses (12 mg/day). Consider backup contraception. 17. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 18. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 19. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 20. Pretomanid increases the risk of hepatotoxicity when coadministered with levonorgestrel oral. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during pretomanid therapy. 21. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 22. Protamines and levonorgestrel oral may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ranolazine levels or effects are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel oral by inducing CYP3A4. Use an effective non-hormonal contraceptive. 26. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 27. Ritonavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 29. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 30. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 31. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel oral by receptor binding competition. Patients must use additional non-hormonal contraception for seven days after sugammadex administration. 32. Tipranavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 33. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use an additional effective non-hormonal contraceptive during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 34. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 35. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 36. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Concomitant use of ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Use caution and monitor. 40. Amoxicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution is advised. 41. Ampicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution is advised.
